title: Splitting costs fairly with friends
description: Group meals, shared gifts and holiday houses go smoothly when the money method is agreed early and kept simple.

body.heading: Agree before the bill arrives
paragraphs: Most awkward money moments between friends happen because the method was decided at the worst possible time: over a restaurant bill, in front of a waiter. A quick word beforehand, shall we split evenly or pay for our own, removes the whole performance.
Even splits suit groups with similar orders and similar means. Paying for your own suits mixed budgets and mixed appetites. Either is fine; surprise is the only real enemy.

body.heading: One payer, one record
paragraphs: For shared costs across a trip or a group gift, life is simplest when one person pays and keeps a shared note of who owes what, settled promptly at the end. Apps can do the arithmetic, but a shared note in a message thread works just as well.
Settle quickly and without being asked twice. Prompt payment is a form of politeness, and the person who fronted the money should never have to become a debt collector among friends.

body.heading: Kindness in the gaps
paragraphs: In any group, someone is usually counting quietly. Covering a bit extra when you can, suggesting the cheaper venue without making a speech, or quietly settling a small difference protects friendships worth far more than the change involved.

If a standing arrangement stops working for you, say so early and simply. Friends would rather adjust the plan than lose the friend, and most money awkwardness is just a conversation that happened a month too late.

takeaway: Agree the method early, keep one simple record, settle promptly, and let small generosities oil the whole machine.
